commands.description: Accessibility auditor mapping a UI surface (screen, flow, or component set) to WCAG 2.2 at a named conformance level, as a per-criterion conformance ledger. Activates when a screen-spec or implemented surface has no ledger, or before sign-off. Do not use for contrast-only requests (use color-contrast-architect for 3+ documented pairs, component-spec when its inputs exist, or targeted-questions for missing evidence), a single component (use design-spec-review), or without UI.
commands.name: a11y-audit

commands.description: Design an eval plan for a product AI feature: success criteria, a held-out labeled dataset, per-criterion grading (code-based, then LLM-based), and a pass threshold. Use when a task ships or changes a feature with non-deterministic model output (classification, extraction, summarization, ranking, agent action) needing a repeatable dataset eval, not only example tests. Do not use for non-model features (use test-strategy), Fhorja's own command outputs (use verify-against-rubric), or with no task folder.
commands.name: ai-feature-eval-harness

commands.description: Review an API contract (shapes, errors, auth model) BEFORE implementation for naming, versioning, pagination, idempotency, and fit with existing endpoints. Use when designing or changing endpoints. Do not use when the API is already implemented (use review-hard or repo-consistency-sweep).
commands.name: api-contract-review

commands.description: Verify a built backend HTTP surface at runtime: per route, record the response, assert it against the slice's acceptance behavior, and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED. Do not use to review a contract before implementation (use api-contract-review or graphql-contract-review), write code (use implement-approved-slice), triage a failure (use incident-triage), for a browser, app, or Godot surface, or with no running backend.
commands.name: api-runtime-verify

commands.description: Verify a mobile or app runtime: run the app (device, emulator, or headless), read captured output (logcat, iOS device log, or Metro/JS console), classify errors per stack, and decide a PASS/FAIL gate. Adapters: React Native/Expo, Unity mobile. Do not use to plan a screen (use implementation-plan), to write or fix code (use implement-approved-slice), to triage a failure (use incident-triage), for a Godot scene (use godot-runtime-verify), or with no app to run.
commands.name: app-runtime-verify

commands.description: Persist triage decisions (apply, decline, discuss) into REVIEW_PREFERENCES.md so future sweeps suppress declined findings. Use after editing triage values in a SWEEP snapshot from repo-consistency-sweep. Do not use without a snapshot or before triage values are set.
commands.name: apply-sweep-triage

commands.description: Atomically lock IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md as the approved execution baseline and stamp TASK_STATE.md with the approval signal; the plan-level counterpart to approve-proposed. Use on every plan implementation-plan produces or self-critique-and-revise revises; it self-runs a blinded review, and only an ESCALATED exit reaches the user. Do not use when the plan is still draft, implementation-plan returned NO_OP, the plan contains [NEEDS CLARIFICATION:] markers, or revisions are pending review.
commands.name: approve-plan

commands.description: Atomically persist every file marked PROPOSED in the most recent prior assistant turn's `### Artifact changes` block, promoting staged content to real files. Invoked on request only. Use when that block contained files marked PROPOSED and you have accepted the inline content of each. Do not use when the prior turn had no such block, every artifact is APPLIED or SKIP, you have not read the proposed content, or you want to approve only a subset (run the original command in Agent mode).
commands.name: approve-proposed

commands.description: Produce ATOM_AUDIT.md table auditing every atom component against COMPONENT_GUIDELINES.md (memo, callbacks, inline styles, touch target, a11y, reduced motion). Use when 2-4 weeks have passed since last audit, 5+ new atoms shipped, or COMPONENT_GUIDELINES has a new normative rule. Do not use when no atoms exist (run design-bootstrap first), for a single atom (use design-spec-review instead), or for 6 or more atoms (use atom-audit-fleet).
commands.name: atom-audit

commands.description: Audit every atom in parallel against the component guidelines, one worker per small group, merging rows into one ATOM_AUDIT.md table (orchestrator-workers variant of atom-audit). Use when the atom count is 6 or more and COMPONENT_GUIDELINES.md exists. Do not use below 6 atoms (use atom-audit single-agent), without COMPONENT_GUIDELINES.md, or when only 1 or 2 atoms changed (use design-spec-review per component).
commands.name: atom-audit-fleet

commands.description: Read-only board of an autonomous-run task: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN waves and slices and TASK_STATE phases as to-do, in-progress, escalated, proposed, done columns. Use when you want a single-glance status of an autonomous run. Do not use to change state (use sync-task-state), to assess a multi-slice task (use where-we-at), or to route next (use what-next).
commands.name: autonomous-board

commands.description: Decide whether an already-defined project is ready to boot an unattended overnight run, and refuse until it is. Emits a per-criterion ledger with a BOOT or NOT-READY verdict naming every missing item. Use before handing a night to autonomous-run. Do not use to approve a plan (use approve-plan), to drive the run itself (use autonomous-run), to view a run in flight (use autonomous-board), or to shape a fuzzy objective before a task exists (use problem-framing).
commands.name: autonomous-readiness

commands.description: Run one approved task in one supervised session with the direct-use reference dispatcher, delegating verifiable slices to existing commands and emitting PROPOSED diffs only and never creating commits or attestation refs. Use when a maintainer invokes Fhorja directly after approve-plan and a BOOT verdict from autonomous-readiness. Do not use inside another execution loop, for an unapproved or NOT-READY plan, a single slice (use implement-approved-slice), or when durable resume, sandboxing, credentials, remote control, commit, publication, merge, or deploy is needed.
commands.name: autonomous-run

commands.description: Produce a staff-grade backend system-design RFC: a 12-section document for a new service, endpoint, or feature. Composes with slo-define, performance-budget, api-contract-review, release-plan. Use when a backend feature needs architecture-level design before planning. Do not use to slice a designed change (use implementation-plan), for blast radius (use impact-analysis), a lone API contract (use api-contract-review), the frontend (use frontend-system-design), or with no task folder (run task-init).
commands.name: backend-system-design

commands.description: Return a branch name and concise commit message (max 3 lines) for the current task, grounded in the real `git diff`; with `--apply`, create the commit after showing the staged diff. Use when the user only needs quick branch and commit naming before committing, PR packaging is unnecessary, and a real diff exists; use `--apply` when the closure floor needs a commit. Do not use when a full PR package is needed (use pr-package), there is no diff yet, or the diff is too unclear.
commands.name: branch-commit

commands.description: Append one observation, question, hypothesis, or concern to TASK_STATE.md as lean, append-only task memory, leaving other artifacts and work undisturbed. Use when something surfaces mid-work, a hypothesis needs logging, or a concern is too small for decision-interview or targeted-questions. Do not use for a decision (use decision-interview or sync-task-state), a new direction (use direction-adjust), multi-artifact changes (use state-reconcile), or with no task (run task-init).
commands.name: capture-observation

commands.description: Pull references (URLs or topics) from the web, summarize each with a freshness format, and append them to the project's REFERENCES.md for later tasks. Use when the user persists project-level references, supplies URLs, has a reference that outlives the task, or seeds REFERENCES.md. Do not use when the project folder is missing (run project-bootstrap), the input is task-internal, a codebase observation (use capture-observation), or a decision (use decision-interview or direction-adjust).
commands.name: capture-references

commands.description: Generate and re-sync an AI-readable code context map (ranked, token-budgeted Markdown of files, imports, signatures, and typed boundary calls) for a target project (or, from a seed file, its import chain). Opt-in; not part of default task init. Use when fast structural orientation is needed before editing, when onboarding to an unfamiliar repo, or when an existing map is stale. Do not use to locate one behavior (use code-locate), for blast radius (use impact-analysis), for a database schema (use db-context-supabase), or without a target codebase path.
commands.name: code-context-map

commands.description: Locate code paths and line ranges for a described behavior: up to 10 candidates with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence and a search trail, plus a proposed SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md update. Use when the first question is where one specific behavior lives and paths are unknown. Do not use when paths are explicit, the codebase is tiny and known, for a whole-repo overview or skeleton, or for architectural understanding (use impact-analysis).
commands.name: code-locate

commands.description: Audit contrast pairs against WCAG 2.2 AA and AAA before visuals lock, with a matrix and token fixes. Activates when design-bootstrap proposes tokens without contrast pairs, or screen-spec or component-spec has an unvalidated pair. Do not use for a single pair (use component-spec), with no accessibility target (use decision-interview), or after remediation is agreed (use implement-approved-slice).
commands.name: color-contrast-architect

commands.description: Produce a lossy compaction of TASK_STATE.md when task memory outgrows a useful size, keeping canonical decisions and the next step, dropping stale facts. Use when memory spans 5+ completed slices and feels heavy, resume cost grows, known facts are mostly resolved, or before a session pause. Do not use in early discovery, when artifacts disagree (use state-reconcile first), when a sync suffices (use sync-task-state), or with no task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: compact-task-memory

commands.description: Generate a 15-section component specification from a Figma component using MCP tools, matching the COMPONENT_SPEC.md template and pre-filled from Figma. Use when documenting a design system component. Do not use when the component has no Figma representation or the spec already exists (edit manually instead).
commands.name: component-spec

commands.description: Harden the current decision set into a normative source of truth with no residual ambiguity, saved in DECISIONS.md and TASK_STATE.md as reviewable edits. Use when decisions are resolved, the contract direction is stable, and wording needs hardening before planning or implementation. Do not use when major ambiguities remain, the task needs decision-interview or resolve-contract-gaps, or it is in broad discovery.
commands.name: contract-signoff

commands.description: Validate that a non-Supabase Postgres database (Cloud SQL, RDS, self-hosted) is reachable, introspect a scoped subset of its schema, and persist it as DB_CONTEXT.md. Read-only, opt-in. Use when work touches that database and planning needs verified schema, or DB_CONTEXT.md is stale. Do not use without a task (run task-init first), when the task touches no database, for Supabase (use db-context-supabase), or to record a schema decision (use decision-interview).
commands.name: db-context-postgres

commands.description: Validate that a Supabase MCP server is reachable, introspect a subset of the database (tables, columns, RLS policies), and persist it as DB_CONTEXT.md. Read-only, never destructive SQL. Falls back to the local Supabase CLI when no MCP server is reachable. Use when the task touches Supabase data, schema or RLS and planning needs verified schema. Do not use without a task folder (run task-init first), when not Supabase, or to record a schema decision (use decision-interview).
commands.name: db-context-supabase

commands.description: Ask the minimum decision questions needed before turning the task into canonical implementation rules, on behavior, data integrity, rollout safety, or test strategy. Use when missing information is decision-driven (not factual) or undecided policy blocks planning; in an attended chain it records an open decision as provisional and continues. Do not use for factual gaps (use targeted-questions), when decisions are locked, or when implementation has no correctness-critical ambiguity. To harden wording use contract-signoff; for contradictory rules use resolve-contract-gaps.
commands.name: decision-interview

commands.description: Generate an outward-facing delivery artifact (executive summary, slack or email update, demo script, release note, blog post draft) per audience and format, grounded in task artifacts with no invented claims. Use when delivery needs audience-specific framing beyond a PR description or team status note. Do not use for a code reviewer (use pr-package), a quick team status update (use team-update), or with no active task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: delivery-asset

commands.description: Bootstrap a design system from a Figma file via MCP: extract token variables, identify components, scaffold foundation docs and a component inventory. Use when starting a new project with a Figma file. Do not use when docs exist or there is no Figma file.
commands.name: design-bootstrap

commands.description: Review a component or screen against its spec (variants, states, accessibility, tokens). Distinct from review-hard (general risk) and repo-consistency-sweep (pattern matching). Activates when a slice's Scope touches a design-system component with no cited design-spec-review pass. Use when an implemented component or screen must match its spec. Do not use when no spec exists (write one with component-spec or screen-spec).
commands.name: design-spec-review

commands.description: Capture a small-to-medium course correction found mid-task in your own work: record a D-N entry in DECISIONS.md, update TASK_STATE.md, and route back to the command. Use when it is worth recording, does not invalidate the whole approach, and the current slice stays recoverable with a small plan change. Do not use for PR feedback (use pr-feedback-ingest or post-review-pivot), scope invalidation (use task-init), trivia (use capture-observation), loops (use im-stuck), or reopened decisions (use decision-interview).
commands.name: direction-adjust

commands.description: Synthesize multiple external sources into a task-scoped EXTERNAL_RESEARCH.md grounded in REFERENCES.md, with comparative analysis and a recommendation. Use when sources need synthesis, not capture. Do not use for one source or project research (use capture-references), internal questions (use code-locate or impact-analysis), or no task (run task-init first). For 3+ angles, use external-research-fleet.
commands.name: external-research

commands.description: Orchestrator-workers variant of external-research: parallel workers each synthesize one angle of a research question, merged into one EXTERNAL_RESEARCH.md. Use when the research question has N >= 3 distinct angles or source-groups AND would benefit from parallel deep reads. Do not use when 1-3 sources suffice (use external-research inline), when one source already dominates (no parallelism gain), or when sources have not yet been captured (run capture-references first).
commands.name: external-research-fleet

commands.description: Extract canonical foundations docs (color, typography, spacing, radii) from a batch of existing SCREEN_SPECs. Re-runs only add new tokens and route conflicts to a Review queue. Use when SCREEN_SPECs already document raw values and need converging into role tokens. Do not use when foundations are already curated and screens already reference role tokens (run foundation-audit instead).
commands.name: extract-foundations-from-screens

commands.description: Research and recommend vetted libraries per feature problem (lists, camera, forms, keyboard, sheets), ranked by adoption signal, writing FEATURE_LIBRARIES.md from captured REFERENCES.md sources. Use when the stack is chosen and you want per-feature libraries vetted. Do not use to pick stack layers (use stack-recommend), check framework patterns (use stack-currency-check), synthesize captured sources (use external-research), or without a task (run task-init first). For more than 3 feature problems needing a deep sweep, use feature-library-scout-fleet.
commands.name: feature-library-scout

commands.description: Orchestrator-workers variant of feature-library-scout for deep per-feature-problem library research. One worker per problem ranks libraries by adoption signal. Use when over 3 distinct feature problems each need a deep read. Do not use for 1 to 3 problems (use feature-library-scout), stack layers (use stack-recommend), framework pattern currency (use stack-currency-check), or with no task folder (run task-init).
commands.name: feature-library-scout-fleet

commands.description: Compare design tokens in code against foundation docs and optionally Figma variables to detect drift (undocumented tokens, tokens missing in code, value mismatches). Use when the design system has evolved and foundations need a sync check. Do not use when no foundation docs exist (run design-bootstrap first).
commands.name: foundation-audit

commands.description: Review a frontend architecture at scale, gating micro-frontend adoption BEFORE building (default: modular monolith until 3 or more independently deploying teams and real coordination pain exist). Do not use to design one system (use frontend-system-design), to review a GraphQL or REST contract (use graphql-contract-review or api-contract-review), or with no active task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: frontend-architecture-review

commands.description: Produce a frontend system-design RFC for the active task (12 sections, web and mobile) as FRONTEND_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md, with an --interview mode for interview rounds. Do not use to frame the problem (use problem-framing), to slice a designed change (use implementation-plan), for blast radius (use impact-analysis), for an API contract alone (use api-contract-review), or without a task (run task-init first).
commands.name: frontend-system-design

commands.description: Verify a built Godot 2D or 3D scene at runtime: run it, read the debugger output, classify errors against a Godot taxonomy, decide a PASS/FAIL gate. Real output is the evidence. Use after a Godot slice is implemented, to gate runtime behavior. Do not use to plan a scene (use godot-scene-plan), write or fix code (use implement-approved-slice or implement-slice-complement), triage a failure (use incident-triage), or with no scene to run.
commands.name: godot-runtime-verify

commands.description: Plan the Godot scene and node structure for a 2D or 3D game feature before GDScript is written: scene tree, nodes, autoloads, signals, input map. A 3D plan SHALL declare its renderer tier. Do not use for game-idea framing (use problem-framing in its game-design mode), slicing a plan (use implementation-plan), blast radius (use impact-analysis), scene verification (use godot-runtime-verify), or with no task folder (run task-init).
commands.name: godot-scene-plan

commands.description: Review a GraphQL schema and a Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) contract BEFORE implementation against a GraphQL checklist (nullability, N+1, cost limits, federation, BFF thinness). Use when designing or modifying a GraphQL schema, a federated subgraph, or a BFF contract. Do not use for a REST contract (use api-contract-review), an implemented schema (use review-hard or repo-consistency-sweep), or with no active task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: graphql-contract-review

commands.description: Scan the session and task artifacts for reusable lessons (what was tried, what failed and why, what surprised us) and propose entries to append to LEARNINGS.md, the produce-side counterpart to what task-init reads. Use on demand mid-task after a hard-won fix or surprising failure, or at closure to sweep a long session. Do not use to rewrite learnings, capture one observation (use capture-observation), close a slice or task (use slice-closure or task-close), or when nothing durable was learned (return NO_OP).
commands.name: harvest-session-learnings

commands.description: Break the task out of a loop, confusion state, or false progress and find the fastest safe path forward, routing to a recovery command and editor mode. Use when progress loops or stalls, questions repeat, the wrong command or mode may be in use, or the user is unsure if it is technical, workflow, or scope. Do not use when the next step is clear, for normal routing (use what-next), or for a brand-new task (use task-init). For a vague prompt, use prompt-shape.
commands.name: im-stuck

commands.description: Generate a design-system spec from an image (screenshot, mockup, or app screen) when there is no Figma source: a component spec (--component) or screen spec (--screen), auto-detected. A gated --gameplay mode (off by default) derives a game MECHANICS_SPEC.md from screenshots and playtest notes. Use when you have only an image and want a structured spec. Do not use when a Figma node exists (use component-spec or screen-spec), for code, or to push the image into Figma (that is generate_figma_design).
commands.name: image-to-spec

commands.description: Understand a requested change well enough to make safe workflow decisions, and persist IMPACT_ANALYSIS.md: blast radius, contract, schema and runtime risks. Use when a task is new or partly understood, or a change may touch contracts, schema, integrations, runtime, or critical user flows. Do not use if a valid one exists, to only sync memory, for an observed failure (use incident-triage), or to implement (use implement-approved-slice). Greenfield: backend-system-design, frontend-architecture-review, ai-feature-eval-harness, code-context-map.
commands.name: impact-analysis

commands.description: Implement only the approved slice with minimal changes, then persist execution evidence in slice notes and TASK_STATE.md. The official execution path. Opt-in test-first mode via --tdd. Use when the plan and slice are approved, ambiguity is resolved and files in scope are known. Do not use during discovery or planning, with open ambiguity, only to sync memory or close a slice (use sync-task-state or slice-closure), or a micro-delta (use implement-slice-complement).
commands.name: implement-approved-slice

commands.description: Orchestrator-workers variant of implement-approved-slice that runs independent approved slices in parallel, one worktree-isolated worker per slice per wave, merged after each wave. Use when the active task has an approved multi-slice plan whose Execution waves show at least one wave of size 2 or more. Do not use when the slice DAG is a pure chain (use implement-approved-slice), when slices are unapproved, when Scope/Depends-on are not declared in the plan, or for single-slice tasks.
commands.name: implement-fleet

commands.description: Execute a bounded micro-delta (fixes, polish, missed checklist items) inside the same slice intent and locked decisions, with evidence in slice notes. Use when a slice is implemented or ready-to-close-with-follow-ups and a narrow gap (bug, typo, test, log line, copy, refactor) fits a numbered micro-delta list over named files. Do not use for net-new scope (use implementation-plan), ambiguity (use targeted-questions or decision-interview), changed signed-off decisions (use post-review-pivot), memory updates (use sync-task-state), or closure judgment (use slice-closure).
commands.name: implement-slice-complement

commands.description: Define an incremental plan for the active task as IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md plus a TASK_STATE.md update: smallest safe slices with scope, validation and exit criteria. No code is written. A --spec mode derives slices from a spec or PRD. A retrofit mode annotates in-progress plans so they can adopt implement-fleet. Do not use when the task is too unclear, facts or decisions are open, or to implement an approved slice (use implement-approved-slice).
commands.name: implementation-plan

commands.description: Triage a concrete technical failure (stack trace, failing test, runtime symptom, production alert), classify it and pick a fix size (HOTFIX/SLICE/INVESTIGATION/ESCALATE). Use when there is concrete failure evidence, an active task folder exists, and urgency is real or unclear, or hotfix versus full flow is unclear. Do not use when it is not concrete (use im-stuck or what-next), feature-shaped (use task-init), already fixed (use pr-package), from PR feedback (use pr-feedback-ingest or post-review-pivot), or no task folder exists.
commands.name: incident-triage

commands.description: Identify the invariants, non-goals, and forbidden changes for the task and persist them, locking implementation boundaries before planning or coding. Use when impact analysis is done or mostly clear and the task may touch sensitive behavior, contracts, schema, or runtime. Do not use when the task is too unclear, facts missing (use targeted-questions), or boundaries are locked.
commands.name: invariants-and-non-goals

commands.description: Snapshot the Figma component library (name, tier, node ID, spec/code/story status per component) with a delta vs the previous snapshot. Use after a Figma update or to seed the inventory. Do not use without a Figma source or for one component (use design-spec-review).
commands.name: inventory-snapshot

commands.description: Document a user journey from screen references and a user story: outcome, screen flow, components consumed, critical states, accessibility, security, performance. Use when mapping a user flow across screens. Do not use for a single screen (use screen-spec) or a reusable pattern (use pattern-doc).
commands.name: journey-map

commands.description: Product researcher running Jobs-to-be-Done switch interviews to surface the four adoption forces (push, pull, anxiety, habit) and the trigger, struggle and switch timeline. Activates when PMF or user research lacks methodology, or a decision rests on assumed motivation. Do not use for solo ideation with no user pool, prior interviews, technical blockers (use decision-interview), desk research (use external-research) or surveys.
commands.name: jtbd-switch-interviewer

commands.description: Read-only inspection of a third-party MCP server BEFORE it is added or trusted: scans tool descriptions and scopes for poisoning, returns an add, decline or sandbox verdict for a human. Never installs. Do not use to vet a skill or plugin (use skill-vet), to review first-party code (use review-hard or security-review), or to fetch a remote server definition (record its origin via capture-references, then get a local copy out of band).
commands.name: mcp-server-vet

commands.description: Audits DDL for production-unsafe patterns BEFORE a migration is applied (NOT NULL without backfill, blocking index builds). Activates on schema changes or migrations in scope, or a schema change with no rollback or two-phase strategy. Do not use for trivial migrations on small tables, changes reversible in under a minute with a documented backout, code-risk review (use review-hard), or RLS posture (use rls-auth-boundary-auditor).
commands.name: migration-safety-steward

commands.description: Document a reusable UX pattern (empty state, error handling, confirmation dialog, search-filter-sort, loading skeleton) used across multiple screens and projects. Use when formalizing a recurring UX solution. Do not use for one component (use component-spec) or a project journey (use journey-map).
commands.name: pattern-doc

commands.description: Declares the numeric budgets a change must hold (Core Web Vitals, latency percentiles, bundle size, frame budget) and the action on regression. Spec-only. Activates when a performance-sensitive surface changes with no numeric budget, or before delivering a latency- or size-sensitive change. Do not use without a performance surface, for functional test selection (use test-strategy), or post-deploy verification (use post-deploy-verifier).
commands.name: performance-budget

commands.description: Read-only cross-task board across every active task in all projects: classifies each task and renders one ranked board with a recommended next action per row. An --outcomes mode reports closed-task outcomes instead. Use when you have many concurrent active tasks and want to see whose move it is and what has gone quiet, which task to pick up next, or which should be closed. Do not use for routing inside one active task (use what-next), a deep checkpoint of one task (use where-we-at), or changing task state (it never writes).
commands.name: portfolio-review

commands.description: Per-slice post-deploy verification plan: acceptance criteria mapped to live signals, plus rollback triggers. Activates after a deploy with no plan, when branch-commit made a deploy without checks, or when slice-closure would close a slice without one. Do not use before the slice ships (use verify-against-rubric), for docs-only slices, or when verification exists and the deploy is unchanged.
commands.name: post-deploy-verifier

commands.description: Capture what a PR or team review changed about the intended approach, separate keep from revert, and update task memory. Does not implement product code. Use when review changes direction (wrong fields or migrations) or a pivot digest is needed. Do not use for corrective feedback (use pr-feedback-ingest), when there is no concrete review signal yet, trivial fixes (use implement-approved-slice), memory drift (use state-reconcile or sync-task-state) or new work.
commands.name: post-review-pivot

commands.description: Blameless postmortem for a resolved incident: timeline, contributing causes, SLO impact, action items. Activates when incident-triage resolved an escalation or significant hotfix with root cause, when task-close ends an incident task, or for a notable outage. Do not use for live triage (use incident-triage), its inline reflexion, or no significant incident.
commands.name: postmortem-author

commands.description: Turn PR feedback (Greptile, CI, bots, humans) into a traceable backlog, so the next step is a narrow implement-approved-slice. Corrective scope only. Use when a PR has review feedback to map to files and slices. Do not use for a new direction or contract (use post-review-pivot), no payload, or task-memory drift only (use state-reconcile or sync-task-state).
commands.name: pr-feedback-ingest

commands.description: Prepare a GitHub PR delivery package (branch, commits, PR title and body, reviewer notes) from the real git diff against an explicit base branch, persisted as PR_PACKAGE.md, never inventing work outside the diff. Use when scope is done and diff is stable. Do not use mid-implementation, for a branch name (use branch-commit), review feedback (use pr-feedback-ingest or post-review-pivot), or just slice closure (use slice-closure). Then use self-critique-and-revise.
commands.name: pr-package

commands.description: Run a short socratic intake questioning whether the stated problem is the right one BEFORE a task exists, then write a BRIEF.md that task-init consumes. Use when an objective is fuzzy, broad, or possibly mis-scoped. Do not use for a one-sentence objective (run task-init), a bug fix or hotfix (use task-init), a decision gap (use decision-interview), or missing facts (use targeted-questions).
commands.name: problem-framing

commands.description: Initialize a new project context before any task exists: project folder, charter file, references skeleton, and active/ and archive/ folders for tasks. Use when starting a brand-new project, product, initiative, or client engagement with no project folder yet, or when project-level context is needed before the first task. Do not use when the project folder exists (use task-init), for external references (use capture-references), or for task-scoped work too small for bootstrap.
commands.name: project-bootstrap

commands.description: Shape the best prompt for the current task and workflow phase, matching the editor mode and the command's required inputs, as a copy-paste-ready handoff. Use when the prompt is too vague or lacks required inputs for the next action, or a copy-paste-ready prompt is wanted. Do not use when the prompt is already explicit, the blocker is missing facts or policy (use targeted-questions or decision-interview), for loop or confusion recovery (use im-stuck), or phase explanation (use workflow-guide).
commands.name: prompt-shape

commands.description: Design a pre-deploy release and rollout strategy: pick the pattern (feature flag, canary, blue-green, or progressive delivery) by risk, then specify the exposure ramp, promotion metric and threshold, and rollback trigger. Designs the rollout, never executes it. Gated --godot-mobile and --godot-desktop modes plan a store or desktop ship. Use when a change nears deploy and needs a deliberate rollout. Do not use for post-deploy live-signal verification (use post-deploy-verifier) or a trivial fully reversible change.
commands.name: release-plan

commands.description: Defect-class detection for the lower-value half of code review: convention drift, type-safety gaps, security and multi-tenant invariants, operability issues. Runs after review-hard. Checks against a curated bug-class library that grows via pr-feedback-ingest. Use when at least one slice is implemented and you want a consistency check before pr-package. Do not use before any implementation, in planning, or for design review (use review-hard).
commands.name: repo-consistency-sweep

commands.description: Turn contradictory or unresolved behavior, contract, or policy gaps into one canonical decision set, written to DECISIONS.md and TASK_STATE.md as proposals. Use when ambiguities are known, facts suffice to compare options, and contradictions block planning. Do not use when facts are missing, the need is discovery or impact analysis, or decision questions are open (use decision-interview).
commands.name: resolve-contract-gaps

commands.description: Resume the task from TASK_STATE.md and linked artifacts, reconstruct the truth, and pick the next step after a session break or chat switch. Also owns --lost-session recovery (read-only). Use when work resumes in a new chat or a task was paused. Do not use for a new task (use task-init), only syncing memory, or stale or contradictory artifacts (use sync-task-state for narrow drift, state-reconcile for wide).
commands.name: resume-from-state

commands.description: Review the current task changes for correctness, safety, and maintainability risks before slice closure or PR prep, and recommend the smallest safe next step. Use when a slice or task-level implementation was completed, the user wants a focused engineering risk review before closure or PR prep, or meaningful issues need surfacing. Do not use when no meaningful implementation exists yet, the task is in discovery, contract refinement, or planning, or the goal is full external code review replacement. Opt-in --consistency N consensus mode.
commands.name: review-hard

commands.description: Supabase RLS and auth boundary auditor for tenant isolation gaps in migrations and policy DDL BEFORE deploy (write predicates, service_role). Activates when a Supabase or multi-tenant decision has no RLS policy locked, a new table has no policy in slice acceptance, or scope includes Supabase migrations or SQL. Do not use when single-tenant, RLS intentionally disabled with a rationale, for general non-database security review (use security-review), or the current migration set is already audited.
commands.name: rls-auth-boundary-auditor

commands.description: Generate a screen specification from a Figma frame using MCP tools (get_design_context, get_screenshot), matching the SCREEN_SPEC.md template (layout, states). Use when documenting a specific screen. Do not use when the screen has no Figma frame or the spec already exists, for 6 or more screens (use screen-spec-fleet), or to converge raw values into tokens (use extract-foundations-from-screens).
commands.name: screen-spec

commands.description: Generate one spec document per screen in parallel from Figma frames, one worker per screen, merging SCREEN_MAP.md and routes.md from their partials; the orchestrator-workers variant of screen-spec. Use when the screen count is 6 or more, a Figma MCP is reachable, and foundations plus SCREEN_MAP exist. Do not use for a single screen (use screen-spec), when foundations are missing (use design-bootstrap first), or when frames are not yet enumerated (caller supplies number, slug, persona and node id per screen).
commands.name: screen-spec-fleet

commands.description: Security review of task changes: threat modeling, OWASP ASVS L1 checklist, auth/authz flow tracing, dependency/secret scan reminders. Distinct from review-hard (general risk) and repo-consistency-sweep (pattern matching). Use when the task touches authentication, authorization, public endpoints, PII, crypto, or external integrations, or names an auth or biometric change with no security-review. Do not use when nothing is implemented yet or there is no security surface (pure docs, internal tooling with no user data). Opt-in --consistency N consensus mode.
commands.name: security-review

commands.description: Critique a draft artifact (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, SLICES/*.md, or PR_PACKAGE.md) against a locked rubric and revise it. Distinct from review-hard (judges, no revision) and direction-adjust (records a decision, no revision). Use when a draft was just written and a critique pass is cheaper than re-authoring. Do not use when the artifact is outside the locked set, for operational state (use sync-task-state or state-reconcile), for external feedback (use pr-feedback-ingest or post-review-pivot), or before drafting.
commands.name: self-critique-and-revise

commands.description: Read-only safety inspection of a third-party agent skill or plugin BEFORE it is installed or trusted, returning an install/decline/sandbox verdict for a human. Never installs. Use when evaluating an external skill, plugin, or marketplace entry before adopting it. Do not use to audit a first-party Fhorja skill, to review product code (use review-hard or security-review), or to fetch a remote skill (record its origin via capture-references, then get a local copy out of band into a quarantine directory).
commands.name: skill-vet

commands.description: Decide whether the current slice is ready to close, separating slice completion from task completion, and record the result in slice notes and TASK_STATE.md. Use when a slice was implemented, validated or reviewed and may be ready to close. Do not use before slice implementation, during planning, or for overall task progress (use where-we-at). Before closing a long session, use harvest-session-learnings.
commands.name: slice-closure

commands.description: Define a service's reliability contract: SLIs, SLO target and window, error budget and exhaustion policy (spec-only). Activates when a service or critical flow has no SLO, or a target has no SLIs or error budget. Do not use without an observability stack to measure SLIs (use decision-interview), for one post-deploy check (use post-deploy-verifier), or for a live failure (use incident-triage).
commands.name: slo-define

commands.description: Verify that the patterns the model will use for a framework and version are current per official docs, and cache it as CURRENT_PATTERNS.md for the project. Use when impact-analysis flags greenfield work in an established framework, a new project uses newer-than-cutoff frameworks, or that file is stale (>30 days). Do not use for incremental work with internal precedent, stack choice (use stack-recommend), or fetching an arbitrary URL (use capture-references).
commands.name: stack-currency-check

commands.description: Research and recommend a technology stack for the project from official docs and AAA company practices, with versioned recommendations and trade-offs. Use when the stack is undecided or needs validation, a project starts from zero, or an upgrade is weighed. Do not use when DECISIONS.md locks the stack, for one library (use external-research), or with no task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: stack-recommend

commands.description: Detect drift between TASK_STATE.md, task artifacts, and reality (code, tests, diff), then propose the minimum updates. Also has an opt-in read-only memory-lint mode. Use when TASK_STATE.md is stale or inconsistent, plan or slice files disagree, you need a full cross-check before routing or delivery, or you want a one-shot repair pass. Do not use with no task folder (run task-init), for a small update (use sync-task-state), for fast routing (use what-next or resume-from-state), or for broad discovery.
commands.name: state-reconcile

commands.description: Update TASK_STATE.md to reflect the latest operational truth so the task can resume in another session. Lighter than state-reconcile, for incremental updates. Use when a meaningful step just happened (planning, decision, implementation, closure), a slice closed, decisions changed, the task is paused or handed off, or TASK_STATE.md is stale. Do not use when nothing meaningful changed, the task still needs task-init, or the need is broad discovery.
commands.name: sync-task-state

commands.description: Ask the minimum set of high-value factual questions needed to proceed safely, then persist the result in the task repository. Covers factual gaps only. Use when impact analysis or boundary definition found missing facts, correctness depends on unconfirmed information, or planning is blocked. Do not use for missing decisions (use decision-interview), when enough is known to plan, or, mid-implementation, when the gap is not correctness-critical.
commands.name: targeted-questions

commands.description: Close a whole finished task: verify the spec done-conditions, set TASK_STATE.md to its final closed state, and move the folder from active/ to archive/. Use when all slices are closed, the work is merged or explicitly waived, and the task is ending. Do not use for one slice (use slice-closure), unfinished work, progress checks (use where-we-at), memory sync (use sync-task-state), or new scope (use task-init). Before archiving: harvest-session-learnings. Next: portfolio-review.
commands.name: task-close

commands.description: Initialize the task folder and base task memory inside projects/<client>__<project>/active/YYYY-MM-DD_<task-slug>/, seeded from PROJECT_CHARTER.md when present, or from a vetted issue-tracker MCP item (gated, off by default). Use at the START of any engineering work in this workflow's repositories, before the first file is edited, including a one-line docs change or a typo fix (small scope never skips the workflow). Do not use when the task folder exists, to resume (use resume-from-state), or to update memory (use sync-task-state). For a brief with 3 or more independent sub-tasks, use task-init-fleet.
commands.name: task-init

commands.description: Orchestrator-workers variant of task-init that decomposes a complex brief into N parallel independent sub-tasks, each worker running a full task-init. Use when the brief contains N >= 3 logically independent work streams (e.g., REST->GraphQL migration across api-server + mobile-app + web-app; or implement-X for 4 distinct features that share infra but not delivery). Do not use for one cohesive task (use task-init), for sequential dependencies that cannot run in parallel, or when sub-task scopes are unclear (run decision-interview first).
commands.name: task-init-fleet

commands.description: Provision, report, or attach a dedicated git worktree and branch for the active task so parallel tasks do not collide on one working tree. Opt-in, git-gated. Use when a task needs an isolated worktree and branch, or to attach one to an in-flight task. Do not use for the ephemeral slice-level worktrees implement-fleet manages, a non-git project, or closing the task (task-close owns teardown).
commands.name: task-workspace

commands.description: Write a short, natural English status update for any team channel (Slack, Discord, Teams, email, PR comment, standup notes), grounded and professional. Use when the user wants to share progress with teammates or reviewers, work hits a meaningful checkpoint, or a short async note fits. Do not use when there is no meaningful progress, PR packaging is needed (use pr-package), or the message belongs in PR_PACKAGE.md reviewer notes. A gated mode can send it to a vetted messaging MCP after the user confirms the exact payload and destination in the same turn.
commands.name: team-update

commands.description: Define the smallest set of meaningful tests that protects behavior and reduces the regression risk for the active task, persisted as TEST_STRATEGY.md. Use when a change affects behavior, contracts, data flow or regression risk, or auth, biometric or runtime-risk scope lacks one, even if small. Do not use when the change is unclear, for broad discovery or contract resolution, or when too small to justify.
commands.name: test-strategy

commands.description: Plan the Unity GameObject hierarchy and components for a 3D feature before any C#: scenes, prefabs, MonoBehaviour ownership, input model, networked authority for multiplayer. A 3D plan SHALL declare its render pipeline and a multiplayer plan its topology. Do not use to frame the game idea (use problem-framing in its game-design mode), slice a planned build (use implementation-plan), analyze blast radius (use impact-analysis), verify a running build (use app-runtime-verify), or without an active task folder (run task-init first).
commands.name: unity-scene-plan

commands.description: Spawn a stateless, independent sub-agent with ONLY the artifact path, the locked rubric and read-only tools, returning a structured per-criterion verdict. Use after pr-package, contract-signoff, or implement-approved-slice on HIGH-complexity slices needing independent verification; not on LOW or MEDIUM slices (self-critique-and-revise), but always when approve-plan or a zero-finding review-hard dispatches it. Do not use without a rubric (use resolve-contract-gaps) or task (use task-init). For 4+ artifacts, use verify-against-rubric-fleet.
commands.name: verify-against-rubric

commands.description: Orchestrator-workers generalization of verify-against-rubric: parallel stateless sub-agents judge one artifact each against ONE locked rubric, merged into VERIFICATION_LOG.md. Use when N >= 4 artifacts share one rubric (multi-slice retrospective, batch PR review). Do not use for single artifacts (use verify-against-rubric), when rubrics differ per artifact (run separately or refactor the rubric first), or on LOW/MEDIUM complexity slices (use self-critique-and-revise).
commands.name: verify-against-rubric-fleet

commands.description: Verify a built web frontend at runtime: serve the build, assert page identity, run the web battery (overflow 320 to 2560, keyboard, console, Lighthouse, axe), and decide a PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED gate. Fixes are routed, not applied. Do not use to plan (implementation-plan), write code (implement-approved-slice), for perf budgets (performance-budget), Godot or mobile, or without a build.
commands.name: web-runtime-verify

commands.description: Determine the active task's stage and recommend the single best immediate next command, editor mode, and work complexity from task artifacts, without reopening discovery. Use when you need a fast next-step answer from existing state and the next step is not obvious. Do not use when brand new (use task-init), after context loss (use resume-from-state), to compare candidates, or when looping (use im-stuck).
commands.name: what-next

commands.description: Macro checkpoint assessing the real task state against the approved plan and artifacts: what is done, missing, and remaining. Broader than slice closure. Use when the user wants a progress checkpoint, the task has multiple phases or slices, or the need is broader than closing one slice. Do not use for a single-slice task or closing one slice (use slice-closure), a brand-new task with no state, or a fast routing answer (use what-next).
commands.name: where-we-at

commands.description: Pedagogical onboarding helper that explains which command and editor mode to use now, why, and the next 2-3 steps, for users still learning the workflow phases. Use when the user wants a guided explanation of the moment or the workflow, a short recommended sequence, or is new or onboarding a teammate. Do not use for a fast next-step answer (use what-next), when the user is fluent in the phases, or the task is stuck (use im-stuck).
commands.name: workflow-guide
